history.summary: NOT a conventional temple: this row refers to the Banawali archaeological site, an Indus Valley Civilization settlement in Fatehabad district, Haryana, on the left bank of the dried-up Sarasvati river, about 16 km from Fatehabad town and ~120 km northeast of Kalibangan (coords per Wikipedia 29.59833, 75.39194). Excavated by R.S. Bisht of the ASI in 1974 (some sources report discovery in 1973 — discrepancy flagged). Three occupation phases: Period I pre-Harappan (c. 2500–2300 BCE), Period II mature Harappan (c. 2300–1700 BCE) with a well-planned fortified township on a radial street pattern, and Period III post-Harappan/Banawali-Bara (c. 1700–1500/1450 BCE). Finds include seals, terracotta figurines, copper fish-hooks, charred barley, and the notable terracotta plough replica. The CSV 'state' column wrongly holds the town name; the actual state is Haryana. There are no regular visitor hours; access is an ASI-site matter (verify).

name: Banawali Temple Site
town_description: Banawali is a village in Fatehabad district, Haryana, on the bed of the ancient Sarasvati (Ghaggar-Hakra) river, about 16 km from Fatehabad town. It is known principally for the excavated Harappan-period archaeological mound adjacent to the village.
